sources.entry: RSS-Bridge - Generate RSS/ATOM feeds for websites which don't have one. Unlicense PHP/Docker

summary.one_liner: RSS-Bridge is a PHP web application that generates RSS/Atom feeds for websites that do not offer one.
summary.what_it_does: RSS-Bridge is a PHP web application that produces web feeds from sites that lack them. It ships with a collection of "bridges" (447 in total per the README), each targeting a specific site, such as Reddit, YouTube, Mastodon, Telegram, TikTok, Twitch, and The Pirate Bay. It also includes generic bridges: CssSelectorBridge and XPathBridge scrape feeds using CSS selectors or XPath, FeedMergeBridge combines several feeds, FeedReducerBridge thins out noisy feeds, and FilterBridge filters items by keyword. Output can be in Atom, HTML, JSON, MRSS, Plaintext, or Sfeed format. Responses are cached through file, SQLite, Memcached, array, or null backends, and the operator can choose which bridges are enabled. Errors can be shown as feed items, as HTTP errors, or suppressed. Optional token or HTTP Basic Auth can password-protect an instance.
use_cases: Generate an RSS feed for a website that has none
Follow a subreddit, YouTube channel, or Mastodon account in a feed reader
Scrape a page into a feed using CSS selectors or XPath
Merge or filter several feeds into one
Self-host a private feed generator for personal use
Reduce noise in a high-volume feed
stack: nginx or Caddy with php-fpm (install guides)
notable: Large bridge library (447 bridges) covering many social and video sites
Generic CssSelectorBridge and XPathBridge let you build feeds for arbitrary pages without writing code
Multiple output formats including Atom, JSON, and Sfeed
Operators choose which bridges are enabled and can tune caching and error reporting
caveats: Some bridges depend on third-party sites that may change or block scraping; the README notes the Heroku quick deploy currently does not work
Requires PHP 7.4 or newer with several extensions in traditional installs, and a web server setup for production
Self-hosted instances need configuration and a cache directory with correct write permissions
